newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Balladur says Europe in nation's interest.
newsitem.headline: France's Balladur says Europe in nation's interest.

text.p: Former French prime minister Edouard Balladur said on Friday that making France a part of Europe would make the country stronger and he feared a Socialist government would not further this goal.
"What I fear from a (Socialist party leader Lionel) Jospin government is that they cultivate once again illusions and finish once again by failure," Balladur told Europe 1 radio.
"That means not resolving the problem of unemployment...and not being able to bring France into Europe which is a national, almost selfish, interest of France."
"Nothing shocks me more than to bring the country into conflict with Europe. We will not serve the nation without Europe."
"We must have Europe in the service of the French nation, which will be stronger thanks to Europe," he said.
He repeated his often stated position that the French economy needs more economic freedom in order to grow, create more jobs and produce a more equal society.

"If we want to give France muscle, growth and dynamism, we will resolve the problems of employment and the social fracture. So more liberty, that is my belief, which will give more growth and jobs, will allow us to have more justice in society."
